title: How plants and animals get nutrients
summary: Review how plants make their own food and how animals get energy by eating other living things.
keyIdeas: Plants make their own food using water, air and sunlight.
Animals do not make their own food; they eat plants, other animals or both.
Animals are classified by their diet as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica
A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta

activities.prompt: Animals make their own food using sunlight, just like plants.
activities.explanation: Animals cannot make their own food in this way. They get energy by eating plants or other animals.

activities.prompt: Sort these animals by the food they eat in nature.
activities.explanation: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat other animals, and omnivores eat both plants and animals.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about how plants take in water.
activities.explanation: The root holds the plant in the soil and absorbs water containing dissolved minerals.
activities.hint: This part of the plant is usually underground.
activities.sentence: Plants absorb water and minerals from the soil through the ___.

activities.prompt: Match each resource to where or how a plant obtains it.
activities.explanation: Plants take in water and minerals through their roots. Leaves take in carbon dioxide and capture sunlight.

pairs.right: From the Sun, captured by leaves

activities.prompt: Put the steps of a green plant's nutrition in order.
activities.explanation: First, roots absorb water. It travels to the leaves, where food is made. The food is then carried around the plant.
items: Roots absorb water and minerals from damp soil
The water and minerals travel up the stem
Leaves use sunlight and carbon dioxide from the air to make food
The food is carried around the whole plant

activities.prompt: Adrián says, 'Plants eat soil to get food and grow.' What is wrong with this idea?
activities.explanation: Plants do not eat soil. They take in water from it and make their own food in their leaves.
activities.hint: Remember that plants are producers: they make their own food.
options: Plants use nothing from the soil and only need air to live
Plants only eat small stones they find in the soil
Plants do not eat soil; they make food using water, air and light

activities.prompt: Lucía waters two identical plants. One gets sunlight; the other is shut in a dark cupboard. What will happen?
activities.explanation: Without light, green plants cannot make food through photosynthesis and cannot survive indefinitely.
options: Both plants will grow equally because water is all they need
The cupboard plant will grow much faster because it rests better
The cupboard plant will not be able to make food and will eventually wither

activities.prompt: Read the text carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Plants make food using light, water and air. Animals get food by eating other living things.
activities.title: Aisha's garden
activities.text: Aisha carefully looks after her school garden. She waters the tomatoes every morning. She knows that roots take in water and minerals from the soil. Green leaves receive sunlight and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. Using these, tomato plants make their own food and release oxygen. A snail and a blackbird visit daily. The snail eats tender lettuce leaves, so it is a herbivore. The blackbird eats worms from the soil and sweet blackberries, so it is an omnivore.

questions.prompt: Which gas do tomato leaves take from the air to make food?
questions.explanation: The text explains that leaves take in carbon dioxide to make their food.

questions.prompt: Why is the blackbird classified as an omnivore?
questions.explanation: An omnivore eats food from both plants and animals.
options: It only eats tender lettuce leaves
It makes its own food using sunlight
It eats both animals, such as worms, and plants, such as blackberries

activities.prompt: Hugo reads that rabbits eat hay and lions eat other animals. How are they classified?
activities.explanation: Rabbits are herbivores, and lions are carnivores. To classify other species, we need to know their usual diet.
activities.hint: Distinguish food from plants and food from animals.
options: The rabbit is a herbivore and the lion is a carnivore
The rabbit is an omnivore and the lion is a herbivore

activities.prompt: Sort each statement according to whether it describes plant or animal nutrition.
activities.explanation: Plants are autotrophs: they make their own food. Animals are heterotrophs: they obtain food from other living things.

items.text: Make their own food using sunlight
Get nutrients by eating other living things
Absorb water and minerals through roots
Are classified as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores
Release oxygen into the air while making food
Search for and catch food in their surroundings
